rationales.multiclass: Losing the correct category for one fixed risk-group cluster must block release. The smallest five-seed cluster contains 88 of 2000 evaluation entities, giving 11/250 accuracy loss.
rationales.multilabel: Losing one true label's ranking advantage for one complete target pattern must block release. For pattern size B, positive-label count P, population N, and 12 labels, macro-AP loss is (B/P - B/N)/12. The smallest five-seed pattern-label loss is 31400298689/1417242888000.
rationales.multilabel_ranking: Missing one of three true labels in the top five for one complete target pattern must block release. The smallest five-seed pattern contains 285 of 2000 entities, giving 285/(3*2000) = 19/400 recall loss.
rationales.regression: A systematic error of one level in the known 20-level risk-to-target signal must block release. The signal spans two target units, so one level is 2/19 target units.
rationales.forecasting: A forecast that is one time step late must block release. The generated series changes by 1/4 target unit per step, giving 1/4 mean absolute error across all 12 horizons.
rationales.static_link: Missing one reserved true link in the top five for every entity in one complete interest cohort must block release. A cohort has six of 60 entities and three reserved links each, giving 6/(60*3) = 1/30 recall loss.
rationales.temporal_link: Missing one reserved true link in the top five for every entity in one complete interest cohort must block release. A cohort has six of 60 entities and three reserved links each, giving 6/(60*3) = 1/30 recall loss.

minimum_loss_calculation.meaning: These counterfactual fixture calculations define blockworthy losses. They are not actual weaker-training trials or evidence of detection reliability. Release limits remain unselected.

multilabel.scorer_check: Each exact calculation matched the existing macro-AP scorer within 1e-12.
